hardware_answers.question: Can the Pi run four sources at once with the current helpers (two Wi-Fi, one Zigbee, one BTLE)?

answers.answer: Yes. One Python process carried four sources by by-id path (2 Wi-Fi, zigbee, btle) for 10 min with no errors and no re-opens. A 3-minute mix of C local and Python sources was also clean.
answers.evidence:
p10a, 600 samples at 1 Hz: not-running 0, error 0 on all four. Packets: pw0 16999, pw1 16601, pz2 0 (no zigbee traffic; no TXTEST board was free), pb3 8588. Error packets 0. Devices: IEEE802.11 110, BTLE 19.

Python CPU 2.3-5.0%, RSS 24.4-24.7 MB, 17 threads. Kismet CPU 6.3-9.9%, RSS 32.3 -> 35.0 MB. Load average at most 0.19. The helper logged no lost-sync or damaged records.

p10b: 180 samples, all running, 0 errors.

hardware_answers.question: Why did two boards that reported the 1.2.0 app version and compile time not answer START? Does the USB serial number (the MAC in the by-id name) stay the same whatever the firmware, and in ROM download mode?

answers.answer: Partly settled. The USB serial number (the MAC in the by-id name) stayed the same on current, 1.2.0, 1.1.0 and 1.0.0, through six esptool download-mode entries and RTS hard resets. The by-id symlink for D8:0C was never re-created: its mtime is still 'Sep 28 12:35' and it still points to ttyACM2. The published 1.2.0 image, freshly flashed at 0x0 on board A (38:44:BE:BF:D8:0C) with NVS erased, answered 'START <us> <nonce>' on the first attempt in every test (fwcheck, both helpers, raw 'START 0 abcd'). So the earlier non-answer by two boards reporting 1.2.0 is not a property of this image as published; its cause is not settled. The 20x START loop and the NVS backup diff were not run. Board B was not flashed.
answers.evidence: f10.flash120.out, f10.120.start.out, f10.120.raw.out, ls -la /dev/serial/by-id at each step

answers.answer: Partial: in ROM download mode the USB serial number, and so the by-id name, stays the same. It is the same with this project's firmware.
answers.evidence: After 'esptool --after no-reset chip-id' ('Staying in bootloader.', 'BASE MAC: 38:44:be:bf:d8:0c'), ls /dev/serial/by-id still showed usb-Espressif_USB_JTAG_serial_debug_unit_38:44:BE:BF:D8:0C-if00 -> ../../ttyACM2 (p8.out). The 1.2.0 and backup-image parts were not run.

hardware_answers.question: What hardware label and capture interface do Kismet's REST API and UI show with the current helpers: 'Espressif USB-Serial-JTAG (<MAC>)', a C helper capif of esp32c5-ttyACM0, and the Python helper reporting the port?

answers.answer: The hardware label is 'Espressif USB-Serial-JTAG (<MAC>)' in all setups; a pseudo-terminal gets 'ESP32-C5'. The C helper reports capture_interface 'esp32c5-<tty>' for every radio and for by-id definitions: esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM1 -> 'esp32c5-ttyACM1', 'esp32c5:device=<by-id>' -> 'esp32c5-ttyACM0', C remote zigbee -> 'esp32c5-ttyACM2', pty -> 'esp32c5-pts/1'. The Python helper reports the port as given ('/dev/ttyACM3', or the full by-id path). A by-id definition gets the name/interface 'esp32c5', so the C local and Python by-id sources in n9 were both named 'esp32c5'.

For D8:0C, hardware was 'Espressif USB-Serial-JTAG (38:44:BE:BF:D8:0C)' for the C local, C remote and Python remote helpers alike. capture_interface was 'esp32c5-ttyACM2' for both C setups and '/dev/ttyACM2' for the Python helper. UUIDs follow the radio: E5C50001 (wifi), E5C50002 (zigbee), E5C50003 (btle), each -0000-0000-0000-3844BEBFD80C, and are the same in every helper.
answers.evidence: f10rb.out, f10zr.out, f10w.out, f10b.out (kq.py src lines)

answers.answer: The hardware string is 'Espressif USB-Serial-JTAG (<MAC>)' for all three setups: C local, C remote and Python. capture_interface is esp32c5-ttyACMn for the C helper, even for btle, zigbee and by-id definitions. For the Python helper it is the port as written: /dev/ttyACM0, the by-id path, or a /tmp symlink. interface is the definition's name part, for example esp32c5zigbee for 'esp32c5zigbee:device=...'.
answers.evidence: Files: p2.out (a/b/c) and p9.out (d: /tmp/py/board1 gave capture_interface '/tmp/py/board1' and UUID E5C50001-...-3844BEBFC910). Only REST was checked; no browser.

hardware_answers.question: What is the exact --list output of both helpers with the four real boards, idle and with a board in use? What does kismet_cap_esp32c5 --version print for the native build?

answers.answer: --version prints '2026.09.0-cfe427074' (exit 0). C --list goes to stderr, exits 2, starts with 'esp32c5 supported data sources:' and gives 3 rows per board, '    esp32c5-ttyACM0:mode=wifi (Espressif USB-Serial-JTAG (10:BD:A3:CF:05:40))' plus the zigbee/btle forms. That matches the wiki blocks exactly apart from the example MAC. It hides all three rows of a board held by either helper, a C local source or the Python remote helper (both take the flock). With every board held it prints 'esp32c5 - No supported data sources found...' (exit 2), as the wiki says. The Python --list (stdout, exit 0) never hides held boards; the wiki does not claim it does, but could say so.
answers.evidence: n2.out, n2b.out, the all-held run; Command-Line-Reference.md:126, Hardware.md:141, Install-on-Linux.md:196, Install-on-Raspberry-Pi.md:238, Multiple-Boards.md:37, Building-Kismet...md:415.

answers.answer: Exact outputs are in check 1. The Python --list prints to stdout, exits 0 and lists every board, held or not. The C --list prints only to stderr, exits 2, and hides all three rows of a board held by either helper. --version prints 2026.09.0-cfe427074, exit 0.

hardware_answers.question: BLE on the air: is BLE 5 extended advertising not captured? Is SCAN_RSP never captured (passive scan), so names sent only in scan responses are missing? What scan duty cycle does the controller really give?

answers.answer: Passive parts settled; the active parts (own adverts from hci0) could not be run. (1) Extended advertising: none is captured. The firmware uses the legacy NimBLE passive scan and drops any report with more than 31 data bytes (sniff_ble: data_len > 31 -> s_oversize++). In 12,695 records from 6 captures, the only PDU types were ADV_IND (0) and ADV_NONCONN_IND (2), and the longest AdvData was 31 bytes (2217 of 3644 records at exactly 31). No extended advertiser nearby was known, so absence on air is shown but not proven against a known source. (2) SCAN_RSP: 0 in 12,695 records (PDU type 4 never seen), and no ADV_SCAN_IND or ADV_DIRECT_IND either. So a device that names itself only in a scan response will appear without a name (inferred, not shown with a known device). The wiki's 'scan responses are rare' is effectively 'never'. (3) Duty cycle: the scan listens almost continuously. The strongest regular advertiser (0e:0a:43:01:2a:dd, -34 dBm, 100 ms interval, median gap 105.0 ms, minimum 98.9 ms) was heard 1119 times in 120 s against 28 missed events: 97.6% of its advertising events. The largest gap in the whole stream was 197 ms. Weaker advertisers were heard less often (61-81%), limited by signal. (4) The Pi's own hci0 cannot be used without sudo: 'PowerState: off-blocked' (rfkill soft block) and /dev/rfkill is root:root 0664. So there was no own advertising at a known interval, no extended-advert test and no active-scan name comparison.
answers.evidence: hw2/results-ble-oldfw/b9raw.json, b9raw.out, b9k.an, f10raw.json; firmware/main/esp32c5_sniffer.c:542-550, 1175-1183; bluetoothctl show; ls -la /dev/rfkill

hardware_problems_naming_this_page.summary: A radio switch can re-enumerate the board's USB device, and once it left a board silent until a hardware reset; the wiki says the port stays up through every switch on the Pi
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.evidence: n1: 10:BD:A3:C8:7D:54 Wi-Fi->BTLE, 'port closed, reconnecting', ENOENT for 0.5 s, devnum 8->13. After the helper re-sent MODE BLE the board never answered START again (15 s give-ups, re-opens failed for 65 s). A DTR/RTS reset recovered it. n1c: the same board re-enumerated again (devnum 13->14) but recovered after 2.5 s. g4: 38:44:BE:BF:C9:10 'port closed, reconnecting' on zigbee->wifi. Five attempts to reproduce the hang with MODE BLE sent during boot did not hang.
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.file: docs/wiki/Install-on-WSL2.md:303 (and Choosing-a-Setup.md:120, Hardware.md:155); firmware/helper MODE handling
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.suggested_fix: Correct the wiki: on the Pi a MODE switch sometimes re-enumerates the board's USB device (the tty and by-id link come back within about 0.5 s). Both helpers handle that, so it matters mainly for usbipd/WSL2. For the hang: after 'port closed' during a MODE switch, have the helper try START first (the board may already be on the radio) before re-sending MODE. Firmware side, investigate a MODE command arriving while the BLE stack starts. Record it as an intermittent known issue in Troubleshooting ('board silent after a switch: replug or reset').
